To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
patients who refused any dose of psychotropic medication had significantly higher rates of rehospitalization and restraint use than patients who accepted medication.

overt medication refusal is associated with poorer clinical outcomes, and that patients with a history of overt medication refusal are more likely to have a history of medication refusal, to refuse medications for a variety of reasons, and to have more severe psychopathology.

overt non-compliance (refusal) with psychotropic medications is associated with a poorer clinical outcome, and that patients who are overtly non-compliant are more likely to be male, younger than 40 years of age, have a diagnosis of schizophrenia, and have a history of violence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a phenomenon that is common to all psychiatric hospitals and is a major cause of patient dissatisfaction and staff frustration.
the identification and treatment of patients who refuse psychotropic medications.
the identification of the characteristics of patients who are likely to refuse medications and the clinical sequelae of such behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
non-compliance with medications is associated with a poor clinical outcome, as defined by the need for more frequent and more prolonged use of restraint, and longer length of hospitalization.
non-compliance with prescribed psychotropic medication leads to poorer clinical outcome.
medication refusal is associated with poorer outcomes in patients who are admitted to a state hospital.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patients who refuse medications are more likely to have poor outcomes, and that the most common reason for medication refusal is that the patient does not believe that he or she needs the medication.
medication refusal is an extremely important issue for the treatment of the chronically mentally ill, as it has significant impact on the clinical course of these patients.
medication refusal is a serious problem in the treatment of psychiatric patients and that this problem should not be taken lightly by clinicians. (Journal of Psychosocial Nursing, 37 (4), 16-19.)

non-compliance with medications is a serious problem that needs to be addressed.
medication refusal is a significant predictor of poor clinical outcomes.
medication non-compliance is associated with worse outcomes.
